status: r2 — adds CON/N9001 (Safety & PPE, task T1) to the scored declaration and adds declaration-only signal cards for CON/N8001 (teamwork) and CON/N8002 (plan & organise). r1 only linked the 4 electrical-practical NOS (N0602-N0605); T1/Safety never appeared in match output under r1, which was a traceability gap against the pinned pack (CON/N9001 is practical/task-evidenced, see qp.json). See docs/qp/CON_Q0602_v4_source_of_truth.md for why this is a new rules id rather than an in-place r1 edit.
note: Each declaration item (a picture task card the worker taps often/sometimes/never, or a tool in the tool grid) links to the NOS/PC(s) it evidences, with a weight (0-1) for how directly it evidences that PC. Effective claim strength for a PC = max over its links of (answer_strength x link.weight), where answer_strength is often=1.0, sometimes=0.6, never=0.0 (thresholds.json). A PC with no link at all is out of scope for the match coverage calculation (it can still be scored later from task evidence — see rubric.json) and is surfaced as an unprobed gap, never silently assumed absent. Cards whose links are entirely CON/N8001 or CON/N8002 PCs are declaration-only: thresholds.json's practical_nos_for_matching does not include those NOS, so they never enter overall_coverage, nos_coverage, nos_has_experience, match_result or gap_nos — the matcher surfaces them separately as declaration_only_signals (see matcher.py), never as a score.

known_gaps.note: PCs with no card/tool link are out of scope for the declaration match (they are never assumed absent; they are simply unprobed by the self-declaration and can only be judged from task evidence at assessment time). CON/N0603.PC16 (diesel generator maintenance) is also NOT_APPLICABLE_IN_MVP in rubric.json (no generator on the training board). CON/N9001.PC3/PC12/PC14/PC17, most of CON/N8001's cultural-inclusivity/anti-discrimination PCs (PC9-PC12), and several CON/N8002 PCs are left unprobed deliberately: either not meaningfully self-reportable as a tap-card (PC12 height-pass clearance, PC17 illness reporting), or sensitive workplace-conduct topics (PC9-PC12 of N8001) that this MVP does not reduce to an often/sometimes/never tap without trivialising them.
